questions.q: What is the denary value of binary 1011 0110?
What is hexadecimal 3F in denary?
How many bytes is 1 kibibyte (KiB)?
questions.why: Binary prefixes use powers of 2: 2¹⁰ = 1024.

questions.q: Why does lossy compression make files smaller than lossless?
o: It removes data permanently that is less noticeable
questions.why: Lossy discards some data (e.g. detail in an image); lossless can rebuild the original exactly.

questions.q: An image is 100 × 100 pixels with a colour depth of 8 bits. What is its file size?
How many bits are needed to store the denary number 200 as an unsigned binary integer?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some gave the binary number rather than the number of bits. 200 needs 8 bits (2⁷ = 128 ≤ 200 < 256).

questions.q: Which is a type of compression, rather than an example?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some gave an example of compression rather than a type. The types are lossy and lossless.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal representation of the 8-bit byte 11011010?
questions.why: Split into two 4-bit nibbles: 1101 = 13 = D, and 1010 = 10 = A. Together, 11011010 is DA in hexadecimal.

long.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 3F into 8-bit binary and into denary.
A 10-second sound recording is sampled 44 100 times a second with a sample resolution of 16 bits, in mono. Calculate the file size in bytes.
scheme: A1: = 882 000 bytes

long.q: The denary number 181 is to be stored in an 8-bit register. (a) Convert 181 to 8-bit unsigned binary. (b) Convert 181 to hexadecimal. (c) Give one reason why developers prefer hexadecimal over binary.
scheme: B1: (b) 181 ÷ 16 = 11 remainder 5; 11 = B, so B5
B1: hexadecimal is much more compact and human-readable, reducing transcription errors when reading memory addresses

long.q: Add the 8-bit binary numbers 10110110 and 01101101. Give the 8-bit result and explain what has happened.
scheme: B1: 8-bit result 00100011 (with a carry of 1 out of the most significant bit)
B1: an overflow error has occurred
B1: the true answer, 291 (182 + 109), is larger than 255, the largest number 8 bits can hold

long.q: Describe lossy and lossless compression, and give a suitable use for each.
scheme: B1: lossy compression permanently removes data, e.g. detail the human eye or ear is unlikely to notice, so the original cannot be restored
B1: lossy use, e.g. photos or music for streaming/emailing, where a much smaller file matters more than a small loss of quality
B1: lossless compression reduces the file size without losing any data, e.g. using run-length encoding, so the original can be restored exactly
B1: lossless use, e.g. text documents or program files, where every bit must be kept

questions.q: Which method sends bits one at a time down a single wire?
questions.why: Serial transmission uses one channel; parallel uses several at once.

questions.q: What does a parity bit help detect?
questions.why: An odd or even count of 1s that doesn't match shows a bit has changed.

questions.q: Symmetric encryption uses…
o: one shared key to encrypt and decrypt
a public and a private key
questions.why: Asymmetric encryption uses a public/private key pair.

questions.q: Which method of error detection uses an extra bit added to a byte to ensure the total number of 1s is even or odd?
questions.why: A parity bit (even or odd parity) flags single-bit transmission errors when the count of 1s does not match the rule.

questions.q: Data is sent using even parity. Which received byte must contain an error?
questions.why: 11100101 contains five 1s, an odd number, so with even parity it must have been corrupted; each of the others has an even number of 1s.

long.q: Describe how an even parity check is used to detect errors in data transmission.
scheme: B1: sender and receiver agree to use even parity
B1: a parity bit is set so that each byte has an even number of 1s
B1: the receiver counts the 1s; an odd number means an error has occurred

long.q: Describe the structure of a data packet and explain how packet switching is used to send a file across the internet.
scheme: B1: the header contains the source and destination IP addresses and the packet number
B1: the payload holds the actual data being sent
B1: the trailer marks the end of the packet and holds error-checking data, e.g. a checksum
B1: the file is split into packets that are sent independently; each router sends each packet along the best available route, so packets may take different routes
B1: at the destination the packets are put back in the correct order using the packet numbers

long.q: Compare serial and parallel data transmission, and give one suitable use of each.
scheme: B1: serial sends data one bit at a time down a single wire; parallel sends several bits at the same time down several wires
B1: serial is reliable over long distances because there is no skew (bits arriving out of step); parallel suffers from skew over long distances
B1: serial use, e.g. USB connection to a printer or long-distance data transfer
B1: parallel use, e.g. the internal buses inside a computer (short distances)

long.q: Explain how an automatic repeat request (ARQ) is used to make sure data is received correctly.
scheme: B1: the receiver uses an error check, e.g. a checksum or parity check, on the data it receives
B1: if there is no error, it sends a positive acknowledgement back to the sender
B1: if there is an error, it sends a negative acknowledgement / request to resend
B1: the sender uses a timeout: if no acknowledgement arrives within a set time, the data is sent again

long.q: A product code 41732 has a modulo-11 check digit added to the end. Each digit is multiplied by the weights 6, 5, 4, 3 and 2 in turn, the results are added, and the check digit is 11 − (total MOD 11). Calculate the check digit, then explain how the check digit would detect two digits being swapped.
scheme: M1: products 24, 5, 28, 9 and 4
M1: total 70 and 70 MOD 11 = 4
A1: check digit 11 − 4 = 7 (full code 417327)
B1: swapping two digits changes the weighted total, so the check digit recalculated at input does not match and the error is detected

questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction?
questions.why: The PC is incremented during the fetch stage.

questions.q: Which is volatile memory?
questions.why: RAM loses its contents when the power is off.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of an SSD over an HDD?
o: Faster access with no moving parts
questions.why: Solid-state storage uses flash memory, so access is faster and it is more robust.

questions.q: What is the role of the program counter (PC)?
o: It counts how many programs are open
It holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched
It stores the result of a calculation
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates mostly named registers instead of describing their role.

questions.q: When the CPU fetches an instruction, which bus carries the address from the MAR to memory?
o: The data bus, in both directions
The address bus, one way from the CPU to memory
The control bus, from memory to the CPU
The address bus, from memory to the CPU
questions.why: Addresses only ever travel from the CPU to memory, so the address bus is one-way; the data bus is two-way because data is both read and written.

long.q: Describe the role of registers during the Fetch stage of the Fetch–Decode–Execute cycle.
scheme: B1: the Program Counter (PC) holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory
B1: the address is copied from the PC to the Memory Address Register (MAR) via the address bus
B1: the PC is incremented by 1 to point to the subsequent instruction
B1: the instruction at that memory address is fetched along the data bus and copied into the Memory Data Register (MDR)
B1: the instruction is copied from the MDR to the Current Instruction Register (CIR) for decoding

long.q: Explain how the number of cores, the size of the cache and the clock speed each affect the performance of a CPU, and suggest why doubling the number of cores may not double the performance.
scheme: B1: more cores means more instructions can be processed at the same time
B1: a larger cache means more frequently used data/instructions can be stored close to the CPU, so they are fetched faster than from RAM
B1: a higher clock speed means more fetch–decode–execute cycles per second
B1: not every program can be split into tasks that run at the same time, and cores must communicate with each other, so the speed-up is less than double

long.q: Describe how a solid-state drive (SSD) stores data and give two advantages of an SSD over a magnetic hard disk drive.
scheme: B1: it uses flash memory made of NAND/NOR transistors (control gates and floating gates) with no moving parts
B1: electrons/charge are trapped in the transistors to represent 1s and 0s, and stay there without power
B1: advantage, e.g. faster data access because there are no moving parts
B1: second advantage, e.g. more durable/less affected by being dropped, uses less power, lighter and quieter

long.q: A washing machine contains an embedded system. Explain what an embedded system is, and give two reasons why one is used in a washing machine.
scheme: B1: a microprocessor-based system built into a larger device
B1: that performs a dedicated (specific) function, e.g. controlling the wash cycle
B1: reason, e.g. small and cheap to make in large numbers
B1: second reason, e.g. uses little power / reliable / responds quickly to its sensors

long.q: Describe the differences between a MAC address and an IP address.
scheme: B1: a MAC address is set by the manufacturer for a device's network interface card and does not normally change
B1: an IP address is given to a device by the network/ISP and can change (dynamic) or be fixed (static)
B1: a MAC address is 48 bits, written as six pairs of hexadecimal digits; an IPv4 address is 32 bits (IPv6 128 bits)
B1: a MAC address identifies a device on the local network; an IP address is used to route data to the device across the internet

questions.q: Which translator converts a whole program to machine code before it runs?
questions.why: A compiler produces an executable; an interpreter translates line by line as it runs.

questions.q: Which is a function of an operating system?
questions.why: Applications do tasks for users; the OS manages hardware, files, memory and security.

questions.q: What is an interrupt?
o: A signal to the processor that something needs attention
questions.why: The CPU pauses, services the interrupt, then resumes.

questions.q: What does a compiler do?
o: Translates and runs one line at a time
Translates the whole program into machine code before it is run
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates described the benefits of a compiler rather than how it operates. It translates all the source code and reports errors at the end.

questions.q: A programmer is still writing a program and wants it to stop at the first error so it can be fixed and run again straight away. Which translator suits this best?
questions.why: An interpreter translates and runs one statement at a time and stops at the first error it meets; a compiler translates the whole program and reports all the errors at the end.

long.q: Describe three functions of an operating system.
scheme: B1: a function described, e.g. managing memory: allocating RAM to programs and freeing it when they close
B1: a second function described, e.g. managing files: saving, opening, naming, moving and deleting files
B1: a third function described, e.g. managing peripherals with drivers, handling interrupts, providing a user interface, managing user accounts and security, multitasking

long.q: Describe how an interrupt is handled by the processor, and give two examples of events that can cause an interrupt.
scheme: B1: the interrupt signal is sent to the processor and its priority is checked
B1: the current task is paused and the contents of its registers are saved
B1: the interrupt service routine (ISR) is run to deal with the interrupt
B1: the saved task is then restored and continues
B1: two examples, e.g. a key being pressed, a printer running out of paper, a division by zero, a timer

long.q: Explain two advantages of writing a program in a high-level language rather than a low-level language, and give one reason why a programmer might choose assembly language.
scheme: B1: advantage, e.g. uses English-like statements, so it is easier and quicker to write, read and debug
B1: second advantage, e.g. it is portable/machine independent, so it can run on different types of computer
B1: assembly is used to directly control the hardware / produce code that runs faster and uses less memory, e.g. for an embedded device

long.q: Give two differences between a compiler and an interpreter.
scheme: B1: a compiler translates the whole program in one go before it runs
B1: an interpreter translates and executes the program one line at a time
B1: a compiler produces an executable file that can be run again without the compiler
B1: an interpreter produces no executable file, so it is needed every time the program runs

long.q: Describe three functions of an integrated development environment (IDE) that help a programmer.
scheme: B1: a function described, e.g. code editor with auto-completion, auto-correction or prettyprint (colour-coding/indentation)
B1: a second function described, e.g. run-time environment to run and test the code
B1: a third function described, e.g. error diagnostics that highlight errors, or a translator (compiler/interpreter) built in

questions.q: What does a DNS server do?
o: Turns domain names into IP addresses
questions.why: Browsers need the IP address to reach a web server.

questions.q: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?
questions.why: Data between browser and server is encrypted.

questions.q: Phishing is…
o: fake emails or sites that trick users into giving personal data
questions.why: It relies on deceiving the user, not on exploiting software.

questions.q: In the URL https://www.example.com/shop/index.html, which part is the domain name?
questions.why: The domain name identifies the web server (www.example.com); https is the protocol and the rest is the path to the web page file.

questions.q: An online shop still remembers the items in a user's basket when the user returns a week later. What is the shop using?
questions.why: A persistent cookie stays on the user's computer until it expires, so it survives closing the browser; a session cookie is deleted when the browser is closed.

long.q: Explain the difference between the internet and the World Wide Web, and identify the protocol, domain name and file name in the URL https://www.schoolshop.org/uniform/blazers.html.
scheme: B1: the internet is the global infrastructure of connected computers and networks
B1: the World Wide Web is the collection of web pages and resources that are accessed using the internet
B1: protocol: https
B1: domain name: www.schoolshop.org
B1: file name: blazers.html (in the folder /uniform/)

long.q: Describe the difference between session cookies and persistent cookies, and give one use of each.
scheme: B1: a session cookie is stored temporarily and deleted when the browser is closed
B1: use, e.g. keeping track of items in a shopping basket during one visit
B1: a persistent cookie is stored on the user's device until it expires or is deleted
B1: use, e.g. remembering login details or preferences between visits / tracking browsing for targeted adverts

long.q: Explain how blockchain technology helps to keep a record of digital currency transactions secure.
scheme: B1: each new transaction is recorded in a block
B1: each block contains a hash value of its own data and the hash value of the previous block, linking the blocks in a chain
B1: a copy of the chain is held on many computers in the network (decentralised), so there is no single point to attack
B1: changing a block changes its hash, breaking the link to the next block, so any tampering is detected

long.q: Describe what happens in a distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack, and give two ways a company can reduce the effect of such an attack.
scheme: B1: many computers, often infected with malware to form a botnet, send huge numbers of requests to a web server at the same time
B1: the server is overloaded and cannot respond, so genuine users cannot access the website
B1: one method, e.g. a firewall or proxy server that blocks traffic from suspicious IP addresses
B1: a second method, e.g. anti-malware software on computers so they cannot become part of a botnet, or applying email filters

long.q: Describe how SSL/TLS is used to set up a secure connection between a web browser and a web server.
scheme: B1: the browser asks the web server to identify itself
B1: the web server sends a copy of its digital (SSL) certificate
B1: the browser checks that the certificate is valid and issued by a trusted certificate authority
B1: if it is valid, a secure session is set up and data sent between them is encrypted

questions.q: In an automated system, what does an actuator do?
o: Carries out a physical action such as opening a valve
questions.why: Sensors measure; the microprocessor decides; actuators act.

questions.q: Machine learning is a type of AI where the system…
questions.why: It learns patterns from training data.

questions.q: Which is part of a robot's characteristics?
o: It has sensors, a microprocessor and actuators
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many gave advantages to the owner when asked about the employee.

questions.q: In an automated greenhouse the sensor reading is 18 °C and the stored value is 22 °C. What does the microprocessor do?
o: Sends a signal to an actuator to switch the heater on
Stores the reading and takes no action
Sends a signal telling the sensor to raise its reading
questions.why: The reading is below the stored value, so the microprocessor signals an actuator to turn the heater on; the sensor only measures and cannot change the temperature.

questions.q: Which part of an expert system applies the rules to the facts entered by the user to reach a conclusion?
questions.why: The inference engine uses the rules stored in the rule base on the facts in the knowledge base to reach a conclusion; the rule base only stores the rules.

long.q: Describe how sensors, a microprocessor and an actuator are used to make street lights switch on automatically when it gets dark.
scheme: B1: a light sensor continuously measures the light level
B1: the analogue reading is converted to digital (by an ADC) and sent to the microprocessor
B1: the microprocessor compares the reading with a stored threshold value
B1: if the light level is below the threshold, the microprocessor sends a signal to an actuator (switch) to turn the lights on; otherwise they stay off
B1: the process is repeated continuously

long.q: A farm installs an automated irrigation system that waters crops using soil-moisture sensors. Give two advantages and two disadvantages of the system.
scheme: B1: advantage, e.g. water is given only when needed, so less water is wasted
B1: second advantage, e.g. it works 24 hours a day without workers, reducing labour costs, and responds faster than a human
B1: disadvantage, e.g. high initial cost of buying and installing it
B1: second disadvantage, e.g. a faulty sensor or power failure could damage crops; maintenance is needed; fewer jobs for farm workers

long.q: State the three characteristics of a robot and explain how a robotic vacuum cleaner shows each one.
scheme: B1: a mechanical structure or framework, e.g. its body and wheels
B1: electrical components, e.g. sensors to detect obstacles, a microprocessor and motors (actuators)
B1: it is programmable, e.g. it follows a programmed cleaning pattern or schedule

long.q: Describe how an expert system that diagnoses car faults works, naming its main components.
scheme: B1: an interface asks the user questions about the car's symptoms and accepts their answers
B1: the knowledge base stores facts about car faults, collected from human experts
B1: the rule base stores the rules (IF ... THEN) used to reach conclusions
B1: the inference engine applies the rules to the user's answers and the knowledge base, choosing the next question to ask
B1: a diagnosis is output, often with the probability that it is correct and an explanation of the reasoning

long.q: State the three characteristics of artificial intelligence, and explain what is meant by machine learning, with one example.
scheme: B1: a collection of data and rules
B1: the ability to reason, and the ability to learn and adapt
B1: machine learning: the program can change its own data or rules by learning from experience/new data, without being explicitly reprogrammed
B1: example, e.g. a spam filter that improves as users mark emails, or online shopping recommendations

questions.q: Which search needs the list to be sorted first?
questions.why: Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted list.

questions.q: What is a trace table used for?
o: Following the values of variables through an algorithm to find errors
questions.why: It records each variable's value step by step.

questions.q: A range check on an age field rejects 150. This is…
questions.why: Validation checks data is sensible; verification checks it was entered correctly.

questions.q: What is output? Total ← 0 ; FOR Count ← 1 TO 4 ; Total ← Total + Count * 2 ; NEXT Count ; OUTPUT Total
questions.why: Each pass adds Count × 2, so Total adds 2, 4, 6 and 8, giving 20.

questions.q: A bubble sort puts 5, 2, 8, 1, 9 into ascending order. What is the list after the first pass?
questions.why: The first pass swaps 5 and 2, leaves 5 and 8, swaps 8 and 1, then leaves 8 and 9; the largest value has reached the end, but the list is not yet sorted.

long.q: Write pseudocode that inputs 10 numbers and outputs the largest.
scheme: M1: initialise Largest with the first number (or a very small value)
M1: a loop that runs 10 times
M1: INPUT a number inside the loop
M1: IF Number > Largest THEN Largest ← Number
M1: OUTPUT Largest after the loop

long.q: Write pseudocode to input 20 test scores (0 to 100), calculate the average score, count how many students scored 80 or above, and output both values.
scheme: B1: Total ← 0, Count80 ← 0
B1: FOR i ← 1 TO 20 ... NEXT i (or WHILE loop counting to 20)
B1: INPUT Score
B1: Total ← Total + Score
B1: IF Score >= 80 THEN Count80 ← Count80 + 1
B1: Average ← Total / 20
B1: OUTPUT Average, Count80

long.q: Complete a trace table for this algorithm using the inputs 4, 15, 22, 9, 11, −1, and state the output: Count ← 0 ; Total ← 0 ; INPUT Value ; WHILE Value <> -1 DO ; IF Value > 10 THEN Total ← Total + Value ; Count ← Count + 1 ENDIF ; INPUT Value ; ENDWHILE ; OUTPUT Total, Count
scheme: B1: Total takes 0, 15, 37, 48
B1: Count takes 0, 1, 2, 3, with no change for 4 and 9
B1: output 48, 3

long.q: This algorithm is meant to input five numbers and output their average, but it contains three errors: Total ← 1 ; FOR Count ← 1 TO 5 ; INPUT Num ; Total ← Num ; NEXT Count ; Average ← Total / 4 ; OUTPUT Average. Identify each error and give the corrected statement.
scheme: B1: Total ← 1 should be Total ← 0
B1: Total ← Num should be Total ← Total + Num
B1: Average ← Total / 4 should be Average ← Total / 5

long.q: A program accepts the number of tickets to buy, which must be a whole number from 1 to 8 inclusive. Give one example each of normal, abnormal, extreme and boundary test data, and name a validation check that should be used.
scheme: B1: normal: any whole number from 2 to 7, e.g. 4
B1: abnormal: e.g. 12, −3 or "two", which must be rejected
B1: extreme: 1 or 8 (the smallest/largest accepted values)
B1: boundary: e.g. 0 and 1, or 8 and 9 (the last rejected and first accepted value at a boundary)
B1: range check (and/or type check for a whole number)

questions.q: Which loop is best when you know exactly how many times to repeat?
questions.why: FOR loops run a fixed number of times; WHILE and REPEAT are condition-controlled.

questions.q: What does MOD return for 17 MOD 5?
questions.why: MOD gives the remainder: 17 = 3 × 5 + 2.

questions.q: A local variable is…
o: only available inside the subroutine where it is declared
questions.why: Global variables are available throughout the program.

questions.q: In programming, what is a variable's scope?
o: The region of a program where the variable is recognised and accessible
The total amount of memory it occupies
questions.why: Scope determines variable visibility: local variables exist only within their function/block, while global variables are accessible everywhere.

questions.q: What is output? X ← 1 ; WHILE X < 50 DO X ← X * 3 ENDWHILE ; OUTPUT X
questions.why: X becomes 3, 9, 27 and then 81; the condition is checked before each repeat, and 81 < 50 is false, so the loop stops and 81 is output.

long.q: A 2D array Marks[1:30, 1:4] holds four test marks for each of 30 students, one row per student. Write pseudocode to output each student's number and their average mark, rounded to one decimal place.
scheme: M1: outer loop FOR Student ← 1 TO 30 ... NEXT Student
M1: Total ← 0 inside the outer loop, before the inner loop
M1: inner loop FOR Test ← 1 TO 4 ... NEXT Test
M1: Total ← Total + Marks[Student, Test]
M1: Average ← ROUND(Total / 4, 1)
M1: OUTPUT Student, Average inside the outer loop after the inner loop

long.q: Write a pseudocode function Initials(FirstName, LastName) that returns a person's initials in upper case. For example, Initials("ravi", "kumar") returns "RK".
scheme: M1: FUNCTION Initials(FirstName : STRING, LastName : STRING) RETURNS STRING ... ENDFUNCTION
M1: SUBSTRING(FirstName, 1, 1) and SUBSTRING(LastName, 1, 1) to get the first letters
M1: UCASE used to convert them to upper case
M1: joins the two letters and returns them, e.g. RETURN UCASE(SUBSTRING(FirstName, 1, 1)) & UCASE(SUBSTRING(LastName, 1, 1))

long.q: Explain the difference between a procedure and a function, explain what is meant by a parameter, and give two reasons why programmers use procedures and functions.
scheme: B1: a function always returns a value to the place it was called from; a procedure does not have to
B1: a parameter is a value passed into a procedure or function when it is called
B1: reason, e.g. the code is written once and can be called many times, reducing repetition
B1: second reason, e.g. the program is easier to read, test and maintain, and modules can be shared between programmers

long.q: The 1D array Names[1:50] holds 50 names. Write pseudocode to store all the names in a text file Names.txt, one name per line.
scheme: M1: OPENFILE "Names.txt" FOR WRITE
M1: FOR Index ← 1 TO 50 ... NEXT Index
M1: WRITEFILE "Names.txt", Names[Index] inside the loop
M1: CLOSEFILE "Names.txt" after the loop

long.q: Write pseudocode that repeatedly inputs an age until it is between 0 and 120 inclusive, showing an error message for each invalid age, and then outputs "Child" if the age is under 13, "Teenager" if it is 13 to 19, or "Adult" otherwise.
scheme: M1: REPEAT ... UNTIL loop around INPUT Age
M1: UNTIL Age >= 0 AND Age <= 120
M1: error message output inside the loop only when the age is invalid
M1: IF Age < 13 THEN OUTPUT "Child"
M1: ELSE IF Age <= 19 (or Age >= 13 AND Age <= 19) THEN OUTPUT "Teenager"
M1: ELSE OUTPUT "Adult", with matching ENDIF(s), after the loop

questions.q: What is a primary key?
o: A field that uniquely identifies each record
questions.why: No two records share the same primary key value.

questions.q: Which SQL keyword chooses which fields to show?
questions.why: SELECT fields FROM table WHERE condition ORDER BY field.

questions.q: Which SQL keyword chooses which fields to display?
questions.why: WHERE chooses which records.

questions.q: A table STUDENT has fields StudentID, Name and Form. Which SQL statement gives the number of students in form 10B?
o: SELECT COUNT(StudentID) FROM STUDENT WHERE Form = '10B';
SELECT SUM(Form) FROM STUDENT WHERE Form = '10B';
SELECT Name FROM STUDENT ORDER BY Form;
questions.why: COUNT counts the records that match the WHERE condition; SUM adds numeric values, and ORDER BY only sorts the results.

questions.q: Which data type is most suitable for a field storing a telephone number such as 07700 900123?
questions.why: A phone number can start with 0 and contain spaces, and no calculations are done on it, so it is stored as text; an integer would lose the leading zero.

long.q: A table PRODUCT has fields ProductID, Name and Price. Write an SQL query to show the Name and Price of products costing more than 20, cheapest first.
scheme: B1: SELECT Name, Price
B1: FROM PRODUCT
B1: WHERE Price > 20
B1: ORDER BY Price ASC

long.q: A club stores data in a table MEMBER with the fields MemberID (e.g. M0451), Surname, DateJoined, Age, Fees (e.g. 12.50) and Paid (Yes or No). Give the most suitable data type for each field.
scheme: B1: MemberID: text/alphanumeric
B1: Surname: text/alphanumeric
B1: DateJoined: date/time
B1: Age: integer
B1: Fees: real
B1: Paid: Boolean

long.q: Explain why MemberID is a suitable primary key for the table MEMBER, but Surname is not.
scheme: B1: a primary key must uniquely identify each record in the table
B1: each member is given a different MemberID
B1: two members may have the same surname, so Surname is not unique

long.q: A table SALES has the fields SaleID, Item, Region and Amount. Write an SQL query to output the total of the Amount field for all sales in the North region.
scheme: B1: SELECT SUM(Amount)
B1: FROM SALES
B1: WHERE Region = 'North'

long.q: A table BOOK has the fields BookID, Title, Genre and Pages, and holds these records: B01, Ocean Deep, Science, 320; B02, Star Maps, Science, 180; B03, Lost City, Fiction, 410; B04, Night Train, Fiction, 250; B05, Tiny Atoms, Science, 95. State the output of: SELECT Title, Pages FROM BOOK WHERE Genre = 'Science' AND Pages > 100 ORDER BY Pages DESC;
scheme: B1: only Ocean Deep and Star Maps are output (Tiny Atoms has 95 pages; the others are Fiction)
B1: only the Title and Pages fields are shown: Ocean Deep 320, Star Maps 180
B1: in the order Ocean Deep first, then Star Maps (most pages first)

questions.q: What is the output of an XOR gate with inputs 1 and 1?
questions.why: XOR outputs 1 only when the inputs differ.

questions.q: A NAND gate outputs 0 only when…
questions.why: NAND is NOT AND: AND gives 1 only for 1,1, so NAND gives 0 only for 1,1.

questions.q: What is the output of A AND (NOT B) when A = 1 and B = 1?
questions.why: NOT B = 0, and 1 AND 0 = 0.

questions.q: For which inputs is X = (A OR B) AND NOT C equal to 1?
questions.why: A OR B is 1 because B = 1, and NOT C is 1 because C = 0, so both inputs to the AND are 1; every other option has A OR B = 0 or C = 1.

questions.q: Which single gate gives the same output as NOT (A OR B)?
questions.why: NOR is an OR gate followed by NOT: its output is 1 only when both inputs are 0.

long.q: An alarm (X) sounds when a door is open (D = 1) AND either the system is armed (A = 1) OR a window is open (W = 1). Write the logic expression.
scheme: B1: X = D AND (A OR W)
B1: correct use of brackets so OR is evaluated first

long.q: Complete the truth table for X = (A NOR B) OR (B AND C), giving X for each input combination in order from ABC = 000 to ABC = 111.

A greenhouse fan (F) switches on when the temperature is high (T = 1) and the window is closed (W = 0), or whenever the humidity is high (H = 1). Write a logic expression for F, and state how many of the eight input combinations switch the fan on.
scheme: B1: T AND NOT W
B1: F = (T AND NOT W) OR H
B1: 5 combinations (all four with H = 1, plus T = 1, W = 0, H = 0)
long.ans: F = (T AND NOT W) OR H; 5

long.q: In a logic circuit, inputs A and B go into a NAND gate, inputs B and C go into an XOR gate, and the outputs of these two gates go into an AND gate whose output is X. Write the logic expression for X and give its value when (a) A = 1, B = 1, C = 0 and (b) A = 0, B = 1, C = 0.
scheme: B1: X = (A NAND B) AND (B XOR C)
B1: (a) A NAND B = 0
B1: (a) so X = 0
B1: (b) A NAND B = 1 and B XOR C = 1, so X = 1
long.ans: X = (A NAND B) AND (B XOR C); 0; 1

long.q: A security light (L) comes on when exactly one of two motion sensors (P and Q) detects movement (1), but only when it is dark (D = 1). Write a logic expression for L, then rewrite it using only AND, OR and NOT gates.
scheme: B1: P XOR Q for exactly one sensor
B1: L = (P XOR Q) AND D
B1: P XOR Q = (P AND NOT Q) OR (NOT P AND Q)
B1: L = ((P AND NOT Q) OR (NOT P AND Q)) AND D
